items.title: Home First Finance Q1 profit Up 35% on higher income
items.description: Home First India Finance Company reported a 35% net profit increase for Q1 FY27. The company's operating profit also saw a 33% rise during the same period. Total income for the mortgage lender grew by 19% year-on-year. Assets under management expanded by 26% to Rs 16,938 crore. Gross non-performing assets ratio remained steady at 1.8%.

items.title: Tata group profit jumps 5x in six years as market value triples amid big bets on Air India, semiconductors & digital
items.description: Tata Sons posted standalone net profit of ₹31,961 crore for the year ended March, up from ₹26,232 crore a year ago, while revenue rose 9.1% to ₹42,367 crore. The board suggested a dividend of ₹1,10,717 per share.

items.title: Broker earnings stay under pressure in Q1 as derivatives trading slows
items.description: Most listed brokers saw earnings pressure in the June quarter. Trading activity in equity derivatives slowed, and gold and silver rallies reversed. Motilal Oswal Financial Services revenue surged eighty-eight percent during this period. Angel One and Anand Rathi Share & Stock Brokers reported profit declines. Investor participation remained healthy, but trading volumes were volatile.

items.title: HUL Q1 Results: Revenue rises 10% YoY to Rs 17,149 crore, but profit falls 3% on one-off tax credit
items.description: HUL Q1 Results: Hindustan Unilever (HUL) reported a 3% year-on-year decline in Q1FY27 net profit to Rs 2,673 crore, missing analysts' estimates, as the year-ago quarter included a one-off tax credit. Revenue, however, rose 10.2% to Rs 17,149 crore, driven by 10% underlying sales growth. HUL shares fell over 3% following the earnings announcement.

items.title: Happiest Minds Q1 Results: Profit rises 18% YoY to Rs 68 crore; revenue up 14%
items.description: Happiest Minds Technologies announced an 18.3 percent net profit increase for the first quarter.  Revenue from operations also saw a 14.3 percent rise during the same period.  The company's AI-first strategy is reportedly gaining significant traction and momentum.  A strong and expanding pipeline registered a twenty percent growth over the previous quarter.  Happiest Minds currently employs 6,532 individuals across sixteen different countries.
